A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMRL research by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on Collect, Door-Key and Lava-Crossing, including memory and reward variants, plus oracle-training results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original MiniGrid experiments comparing selection mechanisms and baselines, plus knowledge-informativeness experiments in Table 3 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: v1 uses DQN-based module selection and introduces an LSTM Memory-Augmented Arbitrator. v2 removes that extension, trains the selector and dynamic module with PPO, and implements Gumbel-softmax hard selection and soft mixtures of module policies. Sections 4–5 also introduce concrete rule-aggregation and trajectory-retrieval procedures.

E1.justification: The custom multimodal Collect task is removed. DoorKey and LavaCrossing remain, with additional grid/crossing variants, while Empty navigation is added. v2 also uses Unlock skills and trajectories or skills from several DoorKey and Empty environments as knowledge sources (Section 6 and Appendices A/D).

E2.justification: v1's evaluated DQN, DRQN and DQN+k baselines are replaced by KIAN, KoGuN and PPO in v2. KGRL/KIAN was discussed but not evaluated in v1. Internal comparisons also change from AMRL-ds and AMRL+Mem to hard versus soft AMRL selection.

E3.justification: The retained DoorKey and LavaCrossing tasks change from five and three available actions respectively in v1 Appendix B to seven each in v2 Appendix A. Evaluation shifts from tuned DQN-based configurations to default PPO configurations. New informativeness experiments use 300,000 frames for DoorKey and 200,000 for Empty (Table 3).

E4.justification: v1's selector-reward comparison, memory-extension evaluation and Explore/Avoid-Lava comparisons are removed. v2 instead tests hard versus soft selection and systematically varies knowledge informativeness across low, medium and high configurations on DoorKey and Empty, with results and training curves in Table 3 and Appendix E.

E5.justification: v1 specifies 30-episode moving averages without reporting seed counts or defining across-run uncertainty. v2 Section 6 explicitly specifies ten random seeds and reports means and sample standard deviations throughout its experiments. This establishes a systematic uncertainty-reporting practice; v1's unknown run count prevents inferring an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v1's knowledge-acquisition, prior-knowledge, memory and oracle-training results are replaced by new benchmark and informativeness results. In v2 Table 2, AMRL scores 0.94 versus KIAN's 0.11 on DoorKey 8x8, but 0.53 versus 0.62 on Lava S9N2. Changed methods, knowledge and protocols preclude treating these as same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification changes from generic input-to-action mappings and Q-based argmax selection to knowledge-conditioned action distributions. v2 adds formal definitions for averaging applicable rules, reward/distance-based retrieval scores, sampled hard selection and soft policy mixtures. The MDP/POMDP foundations remain; neither version supplies theorem proofs.

C1.justification: v1's central Memory-Augmented Arbitrator contribution disappears. v2 instead foregrounds concrete heterogeneous representations and processing mechanisms, hard versus soft selection, and generalization/sample-efficiency benefits. Its contributions explicitly distinguish successful soft selection from noisier hard selection, while retaining the overarching heterogeneous-knowledge integration claim.

C2.justification: Memory and modular-reward explanations in v1 give way to interpretations based on combining action preferences and knowledge informativeness. v2 explicitly qualifies the early-stopped Empty results as sample-efficiency differences because eventual performance converges. It also corrects the scaling limitation from selector state-space growth to action-space growth and discusses possible robustness to inconsistent knowledge.

D1.justification: v1's six numerical hyperparameter tables and recurrent-training instructions are replaced by PPO-based architecture descriptions, shared embeddings, network widths, retrieval instructions, rule lists and module-source configurations. v2 references repository defaults instead of listing PPO hyperparameters and newly states that AMRL code will be released upon acceptance. Its main text and appendix disagree on concatenating versus averaging KoGuN module outputs.

R1.justification: v1 positions AMRL against KGRL through online knowledge updating and emphasizes novel memory-equipped arbitration. v2 reframes the distinction around heterogeneous representations and processing, explicitly acknowledges the KIAN inner-actor connection, and adds KoGuN and contextual-MDP discussion. Memory and reward-decomposition positioning is removed; much LLM discussion is relocated rather than deleted.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 adds a traffic-control motivating example, reorders related work, reorganizes the method around module types and selection mechanisms, and restructures the appendices around environments, rules, implementation, experimental configurations and results.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn. v1's detailed architecture diagrams, environment screenshots, hyperparameter tables and oracle plot disappear. v2 introduces a knowledge-taxonomy table, numerical performance tables and newly organized training plots, including appendix informativeness panels. Typography, figure placement and the document template also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis: knowledge-equipped KIAN/KoGuN comparisons address v1's reliance mainly on generic DQN/DRQN baselines, while ten-seed uncertainty reporting and informativeness experiments make the evidence more informative. Concrete module procedures and the distinction between sample efficiency and eventual convergence improve assessability. Reliance on repository defaults and the contradictory KoGuN descriptions limit reproducibility, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantially more relevant and systematic evaluation.
